slides.0.title: The Peloponnese
slides.0.subtitle: Nemea, Mantineia and Patras
slides.1.title: Mountainous: altitude decides
slides.1.highlights.0.title: About 85% mountainous
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Topography is the defining viticultural factor of the Peloponnese
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Altitude brings cool
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Though southern, Nemea and Mantineia sit high, and big day–night swings help keep acidity
slides.1.highlights.2.title: The Achaia coast
slides.1.highlights.2.content: A Mediterranean climate with sea breezes and calcareous soils; Patras wines come from here
slides.1.content: First remember "high = Nemea, Mantineia; coast = Patras", then study each PDO.
slides.2.title: Nemea: home of Agiorgitiko
slides.2.highlights.0.title: 100% Agiorgitiko
slides.2.highlights.0.content: A single-variety PDO with styles from rosé and light young reds to structured Reserves
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Roughly 200 to 850 m
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Low sites (about 200–450 m) are riper and fuller; mid-slopes (450–650 m) most balanced; the highest sites bring most aromatic lift and tension (unofficial zones)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Location
slides.2.content: Diploma essays: use the altitude gradient to explain style differences within one PDO.
slides.3.title: Mantineia and the Patras area
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Mantineia
slides.3.highlights.0.content: At least 85% Moschofilero (the rest Asproudes, in practice often 100%); on the Arcadian plateau at about 650–800 m, one of Greece's coldest zones, with harvests into October
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Patras
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Muscat of Patras and Muscat of Rio Patras
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Sweet wines from 100% Muscat Blanc (Rio is the eastern sub-zone)
slides.3.highlights.3.title: Mavrodaphne of Patras
slides.3.highlights.3.content: A sweet fortified red; at least 51% Mavrodaphne, the rest Black Corinthian; see the sweet-wines lesson
slides.3.content: Mantineia and Nemea are both textbook cases of altitude preserving acidity.
slides.4.title: Monemvasia-Malvasia: a historic fame as a modern PDO
slides.4.highlights.0.title: South-eastern coast
slides.4.highlights.0.content: On the Peloponnese's south-eastern coast, linked to the port of the medieval Malvasia trade
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Sweet white
slides.4.highlights.1.content: A sweet white with at least 51% of the Monemvasia grape
slides.4.highlights.2.title: The name's story
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Ties the history from Level 1 to a PDO of today
slides.4.content: A common question: where does the name "Malvasia" come from? Monemvasia.
slides.5.componentProps.slide.title: 🧠 Knowledge Check
What is Mantineia PDO's main grape?
Mantineia is a Moschofilero white on the high Arcadian plateau.
What does the Nemea PDO require?
What is PDO Patras (excluding the Muscat and Mavrodaphne PDOs)?
A. A dry white of 100% Roditis
Patras is a Roditis dry white; the sweet wines are separate Muscat/Mavrodaphne PDOs.
